finding.claim: deleteAccount computes the delete-permission check and discards the result, so any authenticated user can delete any account, including accounts they do not own.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin User u, choosing id via DELETE /accounts/{id} (route comment at line 19). Precondition: caller is not an admin and does not own the target account.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) takes the caller and attacker-chosen id
a = accounts.get(id) fetches the target by id with no owner scope
canDelete(u, a) is called as a bare statement; its boolean is never read and nothing throws

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) is logically correct (u.admin() || a.ownerId() == u.id()) but its result is ignored. assertCanDelete (13-17) would throw on denial, but deleteAccount does not call it. closeAccount (27-31) calls assertCanDelete at line 29, showing the intended pattern. No other guard exists in this file. Caller authentication, meaning how u is built, lives outside this repo and is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a bool that is discarded by the bare call at line 22; assertCanDelete (13-17) that would throw is never called in deleteAccount, and accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs unconditionally. The only other guard-like call, assertCanDelete at line 29, is in closeAccount, not deleteAccount. The repo contains only this one file, so no route-level or caller-side authorization is visible here.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: src/AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u, a) as a statement and discards its boolean, and line 23 removes the account unconditionally, so any caller reaching deleteAccount can delete any account. The attacker only needs to be an authenticated non-admin, and nothing in the repo blocks that, though caller authentication lives outside the repo and is unverified.
